title: One fever, two names
note: Al-Razi separated smallpox from measles symptom by symptom, founding the practice of differential diagnosis.

research.quotes: heroes.html#f-medicine: 'Abu Bakr al-Razi, about 865 to 925, Rayy and Baghdad.' 'His short book on smallpox and measles... took two fevers everyone lumped together and described, symptom by careful symptom, how they differ.' 'a book called Doubts About Galen, questioning antiquity's greatest medical authority wherever observation disagreed with him.' 'That is the ancestor of every differential diagnosis.'
research.retell: A physician named Abu Bakr al-Razi noticed that smallpox and measles were being treated as one disease, so he carefully compared their symptoms and split them into two, and doctors still diagnose by comparing evidence that way today.

lines.text: One doctor first told two fevers apart
lines.sub: smallpox and measles, both fever and rash

lines.text: Rayy and Baghdad, about the year 900
lines.sub: a physician named Abu Bakr al-Razi

lines.text: One fever and rash look like one disease
He sorts them into two: smallpox
Measles sits on the other side
The same questions get asked of each
He judges by evidence, not by habit
lines.sub: and he writes the answer down each time

lines.text: Every diagnosis today follows that split
Diagnosis by evidence: still his method
lines.src: On Smallpox and Measles, about 865 to 925
